evidence: The two-line 'FORM / FUNCTION' headline plus a specimen portrait commits to one idea: workshop as typographic system.
Space Grotesk headline, restrained neutral palette and single ochre accent read as Swiss editorial, matching the chosen direction.
Asymmetric text column against a portrait, cropped at the top edge, avoids the centred poster-template composition.
One sans family, one accent colour and square geometry are repeated across the headline, CTA and rule.
Voice is confident and editorial; the short date label adds a workshop-poster cadence without becoming decorative noise.
Left text column and right portrait form a clear 55/45 split; the ochre rule seeds the eye at the top-left and the CTA closes the column.
Entry starts at the accent rule, travels down the headline to the CTA, then lands on the portrait and footer.
Headline, subheadline, body, CTA and footer step down consistently; nothing competes with the headline.
A condensed display face for the headline against Inter for running text suits a design-workshop poster.
Display grotesque and neutral sans share proportions, so the pairing reads as deliberate rather than accidental.
The stacked headline breaks cleanly at the word boundary; the colour accent rule aligns exactly with its left edge.
Near-black ground, warm off-white type and one ochre accent keep the palette intentional and print-friendly.
The left column's optical margin is consistent; the CTA plate's internal padding is slightly heavier on the right than the left.
The portrait shows students reviewing type specimens, directly supporting the workshop subject.
Depth comes from the portrait/keyline contrast rather than shadows, keeping the poster flat and modern.
Surfaces are clean; the CTA plate edge could use a tighter optical inset.
The artwork reads finished; the footer's second alignment axis is the only visible rough edge.
The workshop promise, dates and venue are legible in one pass, and the CTA is unmistakable.
Tone and density suit design students and working designers without over-explaining.

strengths: Headline dominates the hierarchy with a 2.9x size ratio over supporting copy
One accent colour used only for the rule and CTA, keeping attention controlled
Text column and portrait balance each other across a deliberate asymmetric split
weaknesses: Footer text establishes a second alignment axis 4 units away from the main column

improvementPlan.problem: The footer lines sit 4 units off the headline's left alignment axis, so the eye registers a second, unintended grid.
improvementPlan.recommendedCorrection: Shift both footer text frames to x=72 and confirm they share the same baseline.
